extracted.intended_audience: patent offices, patent examiners, IP practitioners, policymakers, and patent lawyers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and adopted AIPPI resolution on how to assess inventive step and sufficiency of disclosure for inventions involving AI, including definitions of the person skilled in the art and common general knowledge, and recommended limits on patent offices' use of AI during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'person skilled in the art' (parity for AI and non-AI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of the 'person skilled in the art' should be the same for inventions made by or using AI technology and inventions made without the use of AI technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the skilled person identically whether the invention involves AI or not; do not create a distinct legal category of skilled person just because AI was used in the invention process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person skilled in the art is a hypothetical natural person or team
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'person skilled in the art' should be a hypothetical natural person (or team of hypothetical natural persons) and would use AI technology only if that use would have been expected from the average person in the field (or fields) to which the invention relates, at the relevant date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The skilled person remains human (or human team); whether they are assumed to use AI depends on whether using such AI would have been expected for an average practitioner in the relevant field at the relevant date. This clarifies that AI is not automatically attributed to the skilled person unless routine in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common general knowledge parity for AI inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of common general knowledge should not differentiate between inventions made by or using AI technology and inventions made without the use of AI technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing what is common general knowledge, apply the same criteria regardless of whether AI was used in creating the invention; do not expand or contract common general knowledge solely because AI was involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: International harmonisation desirable for inventiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: International harmonisation of laws regarding inventiveness of AI inventions is desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AIPPI recommends pursuing harmonised legal approaches to inventive step issues for AI-related inventions across jurisdictions to reduce fragmentation and improve predictability.

rubrics_metrics.name: No legal differentiation for inventive step (AI vs non-AI)
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing inventive step, the laws should not differentiate between an invention made by or using AI technology and inventions made without the use of AI technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same inventive-step/non-obviousness legal test to AI-associated inventions as to other inventions; the involvement of AI should not change the substantive assessment of inventive step. (The Resolution does not address examination of the prior art.)

rubrics_metrics.name: International harmonisation desirable for sufficiency of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: International harmonisation of laws regarding sufficiency of disclosure of AI inventions is desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AIPPI encourages aligned approaches among jurisdictions on what constitutes adequate disclosure for AI-related inventions to promote consistency and legal certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same standard of sufficiency of disclosure for all inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard of sufficiency of disclosure should be the same for all inventions. When assessing sufficiency of disclosure, laws should not differentiate between inventions made by or using AI technology and inventions made without the use of AI technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not impose a distinct or heightened sufficiency requirement merely because AI was used; evaluate whether the disclosure enables the skilled person to carry out the invention using the same legal standard applied to other technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent offices should not try to reproduce an invention using AI during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent offices should not try to reproduce an invention using AI technology during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners and offices should refrain from attempting to recreate the claimed invention by running or training AI tools to reproduce the invention as part of examination. This is an explicit recommended limit on examiners' use of AI in the prosecution process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use of AI by human examiners (e.g., prior-art search)
rubrics_metrics.description: AI technology may be used by a human examiner, for example, to search for prior art when assessing a patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human examiners may employ AI tools as assistance (such as for searching prior art), provided the AI is used as a tool under human supervision; the Resolution allows such supportive uses while warning against attempting to reproduce inventions via AI.
